messages:
Anna Lee: Quick follow-up to the packaging RFC — focusing on artifact verification and supply-chain for air-gapped installs. TL;DR: I propose we require a signed manifest per bundle + an offline verifier binary that can validate signatures and SBOMs. Also want to discuss tradeoffs for delta vs full bundles and safe rollback pointers. Looking for ops/security feedback.

Miguel Torres: Do we standardize on cosign + in-toto or roll something custom? Many customers are fully offline so they can't hit public keyservers. I think detached cosign sigs next to tarball is fine, but we need a clear offline key distribution story.

Sophie Chen: +1 on cosign for vendor-signed bundles, but customers will want to bring their own signing keys for internal compliance. We should design manifest verification to accept either a vendor-trusted root or a customer-supplied keyset/policy.

Kevin Nguyen: For delta updates — signed diffs are attractive for bandwidth constrained sites, but applying deltas across unknown intermediate states is risky. Proposal: support signed deltas only for N previous versions (N=2?) and require a full bundle for anything older. Also installer should be idempotent and support `--verify-only` and `--rollback-to <id>`.

deploy-bot: Release bundle 1.12.0 created (sha256: d6f7a8e2...). Signed by release-key-2025.

Samir Patel: We should require reproducible builds and include an SBOM (SPDX) in the manifest so offline customers can audit contents. Also include build-environment pins (OS, builder image SHA) in manifest metadata.

Anna Lee: Agree on SBOM + reproducible builds. Action items I'm proposing: 1) spec manifest schema (fields: bundle_version, artifacts[], sbom_ref, signature_refs, rollback_id, build_env), 2) design offline verifier CLI that accepts manifest + keyset, validates chain (support cosign and in-toto), 3) delta policy: signed deltas up to 2 previous releases, otherwise full reinstall. I'll draft a follow-on RFC with these defaults. :white_check_mark:

Miguel Torres: One more ops/security thing: key rotation. For customers that cannot reach our KMS, we should publish signed "rotation events" as part of bundles or via partner channels (e.g., distributor USB image). Bundles can include cross-signed witness signatures so offline verifiers can detect rotation without online CRLs.

Sophie Chen: sgtm. I'll put together a packaging security checklist covering root key handling, HSM recommendations, and customer onboarding steps for BYOK.

Kevin Nguyen: I'll start a minimal prototype of the verifier CLI and a patch applier mode. Sketch of example manifest (for discussion):

```
{
  "bundle_version": "1.12.0",
  "artifacts": [
    {"name": "runtime.tar.gz", "sha256": "d6f7a8e2...", "size": "12345678"}
  ],
  "sbom_ref": "sbom-1.12.0.spdx.json",
  "signatures": ["release-2025.sig"],
  "rollback_id": "1.11.3",
  "build_env": {"builder_image": "ghcr.io/redwood/builder@sha256:aaa..."}
}
```

Anna Lee: Thanks — I've created tracking ticket OPS-812 for the RFC follow-up and put the draft manifest template there. Please add comments and I'll fold in the verifier design. Ping me if you want to pair on the HSM/key-rotation section. :pray:
